cases.question: What is the exit load if I redeem HDFC Flexi Cap units after 8 months?
cases.expected_answer: 1% of applicable NAV if redeemed within 1 year of allotment.
cases.notes: Question deliberately names a holding period (8 months) instead of asking for the load table directly.

cases.question: What is the lock-in period for this fund?
cases.notes: Open-ended non-ELSS scheme; no lock-in exists and the SID states none. Correct behavior is refusal, not a made-up answer.

cases.question: What is the current expense ratio for SBI Small Cap fund?
cases.notes: Current TER is not in the SID. A good refusal-pointer would reference page 19: 'Investors can refer https://www.sbimf.com/en-us/disclosure/total-expense-ratio-of-mutual-fund-schemes for Total Expense Ratio (TER) details'.

cases.question: What is the max expense ratio the SBI Small Cap fund can charge?
cases.expected_answer: Maximum Total expenses ratio (TER) permissible under regulation 52 (6) (c) is Upto 2.25%. Additional expenses under Regulations 52(6A)(c) * is Upto 0.05%. Additional expenses for gross new inflows from specified cities is Upto 0.30%. Refer to section ANNUAL SCHEME RECURRING EXPENSES on page 17-18.
cases.notes: Answerable sibling of sbi-small-cap-current-ter — same section, opposite correct outcome.

cases.question: What is the NFO period for the ICICI Prudential Bluechip fund?
cases.expected_answer: NFO is Not Applicable for this scheme covered in this SID, as the ongoing offer of the Scheme has commenced after the NFO period, and the units are available for continuous subscription and redemption.
cases.notes: Answer is a stated 'not applicable', which is different from the fact being absent — the SID explicitly says it. Section corrected during SEBI re-map: the fact sits under 'III. UNITS AND OFFER / A. NEW FUND OFFER DETAILS', not the additional-disclosures section.

cases.question: What is the ranking of the fund managers for ICICI Prudential Bluechip?
cases.notes: The SID names the fund managers but contains no ranking. Trap: the question sounds adjacent to the fund manager section.

cases.question: What is the lock-in period for ICICI Prudential Longterm Equity Fund?
cases.expected_answer: 3 years from allotment; this is an open ended Equity Linked Savings Scheme with a statutory lock in of 3 years and tax benefit.
cases.notes: ELSS: open-ended AND locked-in at the same time. Sibling of hdfc-flexi-lock-in — same question, opposite outcome depending on scheme category.

cases.question: What plans are available?
cases.expected_answer: The Scheme has two plans: Regular Plan and Direct Plan.
cases.notes: Answerable

cases.question: Which index is ICICI Prudential Longterm Equity Fund benchmarked against?
cases.expected_answer: The Benchmark of the Scheme is Nifty 500 Index TRI.
cases.notes: becnhmark will usually be mentioned right on the first page, along with the risk-o-meter graphic.

cases.question: How many days until I receive my money after redeeming?
cases.expected_answer: Will be transferred within 3 working days from the receipt of the redemption request or as per timelines prescribed by AMFI in case of exceptional circumstances.
cases.notes: Refer to redemption section.

cases.question: What's the smallest amount I can invest to get started, and what's the minimum if I want to add more later?
cases.expected_answer: Both the minimum initial investment (including switch-in) and the minimum additional purchase are Rs. 100, and any amount thereafter.
cases.expected_section: PART I. HIGHLIGHTS/SUMMARY OF THE SCHEME
cases.notes: Highlights rows XII and XIII, both Rs. 100. Unchanged in the nov-2024 filing.

cases.question: If I put in a buy order today, what time do I need to submit it by to get today's price?
cases.expected_answer: The cut-off is 3.00 p.m. on a Business Day. Same-day closing NAV applies only if the valid application is received by 3.00 p.m. AND the funds are credited to the scheme's bank account before the cut-off; otherwise the closing NAV of the business day on which funds are available applies.
cases.notes: Purchase cut-off p.60; switch-in and redemption rules p.61; amendment-rights note p.62.

cases.question: Where can I check the daily price of my units, and by when is it posted?
cases.expected_answer: NAV is calculated at the close of every Business Day and published on the AMC website (www.hdfcfund.com) and the AMFI website (www.amfiindia.com) by 11.00 p.m. every Business Day. Investors can also request the latest NAV via SMS.
cases.notes: Summarized in Highlights row VIII (p.4); detail section heading on p.66, the 11 p.m. sentence on p.67.

cases.question: How much of the fund's money has to be in stocks versus bonds or other stuff?
cases.expected_answer: Equity and equity related instruments: 65% to 100% of total assets. Debt securities, money market instruments and fixed income derivatives: 0% to 35%. Units of REITs/InvITs: 0% to 10%. Non-convertible preference shares: 0% to 10%. Units of mutual funds: 0% to 20%.
cases.expected_section: A. HOW WILL THE SCHEME ALLOCATE ITS ASSETS?
cases.notes: All five allocation bands identical in the nov-2024 filing.

cases.question: Which companies or stocks does this fund currently hold in its portfolio?
cases.notes: Re-confirmed absent in the nov-2024 filing: no security names or % to NAV tables anywhere; p.17 only links to external monthly portfolio disclosures (hdfcfund.com). SIBLING of icici-bluechip-top-holdings — same question, opposite outcome, because the Bluechip SID includes a dated holdings table and this one doesn't.

cases.question: What is this fund actually trying to do with my money?
cases.expected_answer: It aims to give investors long-term capital growth, with the liquidity of an open-ended scheme, by investing predominantly in a well-diversified basket of equity stocks of small cap companies. There is no assurance the objective will be achieved.
cases.expected_section: Part I. HIGHLIGHTS/SUMMARY OF THE SCHEME
cases.notes: Stated verbatim in three places: pp.3, 13, 33. Unchanged in the dec-2024 filing.

cases.question: Which index do they compare this fund's performance against?
cases.expected_answer: The scheme is benchmarked against the BSE Small Cap Index TRI (Total Return Index).
cases.expected_section: D. HOW WILL THE SCHEME BENCHMARK ITS PERFORMANCE?
cases.notes: GRADING CAUTION — the document is internally inconsistent in three places: cover riskometer (p.1) and performance table (p.14) say 'BSE 250 Small Cap Index TRI'; Highlights (p.3) and section D (p.11) say 'BSE Small Cap Index TRI'. An answer citing either is faithful to its retrieved page; all four pages count as hits.

cases.question: I heard SBI stopped taking big one-shot investments in this fund. Is there really a cap on how much I can put in?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. Fresh lump-sum subscriptions (including additional investments and switch-ins) are discontinued until further notice (addendum dated September 04, 2020). New SIP/STP-in registrations on or after February 04, 2021 are capped at INR 25,000 per month per PAN (daily INR 1,250, weekly INR 6,250, monthly INR 25,000, quarterly INR 75,000). SIPs/STPs registered earlier continue.
cases.expected_section: Part I. HIGHLIGHTS/SUMMARY OF THE SCHEME
cases.notes: Restriction re-confirmed still standing in the dec-2024 filing, same pages (SIP/STP cap details p.44, 'Special Products Note'). Facts live in two distant sections — good retrieval test.

cases.question: Who are the people actually managing this fund's portfolio?
cases.expected_answer: Three managers: Mr. R. Srinivasan (since November 2013), Mr. Mohan Lal (since May 2024), and Mr. Pradeep Kesavan as dedicated fund manager for overseas investments (since December 01, 2023).
cases.notes: No personnel changes in the dec-2024 filing; Kesavan's entry spans the p.11/12 break. Data quirk in the SID: Kesavan's tenure is printed as '0.11 Years', inconsistent with his Dec 2023 start.

cases.question: What single company did this fund have the biggest bet on, and how much of the portfolio was in it?
cases.expected_answer: ICICI Bank Ltd. was the largest holding at 9.68% of NAV, per the portfolio disclosure as on March 31, 2023 (top-10 list excludes term deposits).
cases.expected_section: L. ADDITIONAL DISCLOSURES AS ON MARCH 31, 2023:
cases.notes: Answer is date-stamped; a good answer should carry the as-on date. SIBLING of hdfc-flexi-current-holdings — same question, opposite outcome.

cases.question: Could there ever be a situation where the fund house just blocks me from taking my money out?
cases.expected_answer: Yes, but only in exceptional circumstances amounting to a systemic crisis (market-wide illiquidity, exchange closures, force majeure), with AMC and Trustee board approval and information to SEBI. Any restriction lasts at most 10 working days in any 90-day period, and redemption requests up to INR 2 lakh cannot be restricted; for larger requests the first INR 2 lakh must still be paid.
cases.expected_section: Suspension of Sale and Redemption of Units
cases.notes: The INR 2 lakh carve-out spans the p.109/110 boundary — a chunk-boundary stress test.

cases.question: Say I stay invested for a couple of years and then cash out with a profit — how does the taxman treat that gain?
cases.expected_answer: Units held more than 12 months are long-term: gains are taxed at 10% (plus surcharge and cess), without indexation, where STT is paid — and only aggregate long-term gains exceeding Rs. 1 lakh in a financial year are taxed. Held up to 12 months would be short-term, taxed at 15%.
cases.notes: Rates reflect the pre-2024 regime in force when this SID was written; grade against the document, not current law. UI must carry the dated-document taxation disclaimer (PLAN §3).

cases.question: Is there some minimum chunk I have to withdraw each time, or can I redeem whatever tiny amount I like?
cases.expected_answer: You can redeem any amount — the minimum redemption amount is 'Any amount', and consequently no minimum balance needs to be maintained in the folio.
cases.notes: Stated in passing under the minimum-balance row of Ongoing Offer Details.

cases.question: Once I sell my units, how many days before the money actually reaches my bank account?
cases.expected_answer: Redemption proceeds must be dispatched within 3 working days of the request. If payment is delayed beyond that, the AMC must pay the unitholder interest, presently 15% per annum, for the delay period.
cases.notes: The 15% p.a. penalty-interest angle distinguishes this from hdfc-flexi-redemption.

cases.question: What's the smallest amount I can invest to get started in this fund?
cases.expected_answer: Rs. 100 (plus in multiples of Re. 1); switch-ins are also Rs. 100 and any amount thereafter.
cases.notes: Dirty-data alert: the SID itself misprints the amount as 'Rs. 1,00/-' (Indian comma-grouping typo for Rs. 100); the adjacent switch-in text and SIP row confirm Rs. 100. Tests whether the system reproduces the document faithfully vs. normalizes a typo.

cases.question: What's the smallest amount I can put in as a one-time investment?
cases.expected_answer: Rs. 500, and in multiples of Rs. 500 thereafter. The same minimum applies to switch-ins and additional purchases.
cases.notes: Note the unusual 'multiples of Rs. 500' (not Re. 1) — SIPs by contrast are Rs. 500 plus multiples of Re. 1. A common trap for generated answers.

cases.question: Will the fund charge me a fee when I pull my money out?
cases.expected_answer: No — the exit load is Nil (entry load is also not applicable). Note redemption is only possible after the 3-year statutory lock-in.
cases.notes: Also in Highlights 'LOADS' row (p.7). Contrast case: the other three funds all charge 1% within a year.

cases.question: God forbid, if something happens to me during the 3-year lock-in, can my nominee take the money out?
cases.expected_answer: Yes, but not immediately: on the unit holder's death, the nominee or legal heir (with satisfactory documentary evidence) can redeem only after the units have completed one year from the date of allotment to the deceased holder, or any time thereafter.
cases.expected_section: LOCK-IN PERIOD APPLICABLE TO THE SCHEME:
cases.notes: Distinct from the plain lock-in case icici-longterm-equity-lock-in — this tests the death exception, an edge case buried in the same section.

cases.question: How much of the fund's money has to stay in shares, and how much can sit in bonds or cash?
cases.expected_answer: Under normal circumstances: 90% to 100% of total assets in equities and equity-related securities, and 0% to 10% in debt securities, money market instruments and cash.
cases.expected_section: C. HOW WILL THE SCHEME ALLOCATE ITS ASSETS?
cases.notes: Minimum equity here is 90%, not the 80% of ELSS folklore — verified against the printed table.

cases.question: What is the maximum amount I can claim as a tax deduction under Section 80C in a year by investing in this fund?
cases.notes: The SID never states the 80C deduction cap — p.8 explicitly defers the amount to the Statement of Additional Information. Verified absent across all 137 pages. Extremely realistic investor question whose answer requires knowledge outside this document. A good refusal-pointer targets p.8 (lock-in/tax-benefit section).
